close_reason: All 8 children completed: filter-algebra exclusion rustdoc on 16 types across 7 type crates, plus Filter extensibility README sections in 7 type crates
description:
Propagate the filter-algebra exclusion decision (JMAP-lbdy "Decision: filter algebra excluded", 2026-05-10) into the actual code surface (rustdoc on each affected type) and reader-facing documentation (crate-level READMEs), so that contributors and crate users encounter the exclusion at the point of use rather than only in a closed bead.

## Why this is independent of JMAP-lbdy

JMAP-lbdy is paused on JMAP-sehw and JMAP-yfpq landing first. That ordering is correct for the policy IMPLEMENTATION (adding `extra` fields). But the policy DECISION — including the filter-algebra exclusion — was finalised 2026-05-10 and contributors writing or modifying filter-algebra types today should already see the warning. This epic captures the doc-only work that has no dependency on sehw/yfpq.

The workspace AGENTS.md filter-algebra exclusion section is covered separately by JMAP-lbdy.10 (which has been expanded to include it).

## Scope by crate

| Crate | Types covered |
|---|---|
| `jmap-types::query` | `Filter<T>`, `FilterOperator<T>`, `Operator` |
| `jmap-mail-types::query` | `EmailFilterCondition`, `EmailComparator`, `ComparatorProperty` |
| `jmap-calendars-types` | `CalendarFilterCondition` (calendar.rs), `CalendarEventFilterCondition` + `CalendarEventComparator` (event.rs), `NotificationFilterCondition` (notification.rs) |
| `jmap-contacts-types::card` | `ContactCardFilterCondition`, `ContactCardComparator` |
| `jmap-tasks-types` | `TaskFilterCondition` (task.rs), `TaskComparator` + `TaskNotificationComparator` (filter.rs), `TaskNotificationFilterCondition` (notification.rs) |
| `jmap-filenode-types::filter` | `FileNodeFilterCondition` |
| `jmap-sharing-types` | `PrincipalFilterCondition` (principal.rs), `ShareNotificationFilterCondition` (notification.rs) |

`jmap-chat-types` has no filter algebra and is not affected.

## Required rustdoc content (every in-scope type)

Each in-scope filter / comparator / control-enum type gets a doc comment (or appended paragraph to an existing one) covering:

1. **Exclusion notice** — one sentence stating the type is OUT of scope for the workspace extras-preservation policy.
2. **Rationale** — brief: (a) silent-drop foot-gun at server makes filter extras a query-correctness hazard; (b) `Operator` / `ComparatorProperty` must dispatch on known variants — `Unknown(String)` would be meaningless.
3. **Future hook — IETF-track path**: vendors needing both capability-level declaration AND filterability for custom fields should use `draft-ietf-jmap-metadata` (currently draft-01, `urn:ietf:params:jmap:metadata`). It defines a `Metadata`/`Annotation` companion object keyed by `(relatedType, relatedId)`, with schema discovery via the capability's `metadataTypes` / `maxDepth` properties and a `Metadata/query` filter (currently `textMatch` over vendor string properties). This is the workspace's recommended IETF-track answer for vendor data that needs to be queryable; implementation tracker is JMAP-06zp.
4. **Future hook — pre-IETF escape**: vendors who can't wait for the metadata draft can use the sloppy-value escape (`serde_json::Value` for the filter tree) or fork the per-crate `FilterCondition` type. See `crate-jmap-calendars-types/PLAN.md` for the hybrid sloppy-value pattern.
5. **Cross-reference** — JMAP-lbdy "Decision: filter algebra excluded".

Wording should be consistent across crates (cookie-cutter rule per workspace AGENTS.md).

## Required README content (every affected crate)

Each of the 7 affected crates' README.md gets a brief **Filter extensibility** section, ideally near the existing type table where Filter / FilterCondition / Comparator types are listed. User-facing tone (not just contributors). Covers:

- Filter algebra in this crate is intentionally NOT extensible via vendor "extras" fields.
- Why (one line: filter clauses the server doesn't understand silently break query correctness).
- What to do instead — two paths:
  - **IETF-track**: use `draft-ietf-jmap-metadata` (`urn:ietf:params:jmap:metadata`) which gives capability-declared, filterable companion-object metadata. Workspace tracker JMAP-06zp.
  - **Pre-IETF**: escape to `serde_json::Value` filter trees, or fork the FilterCondition type.
- Cross-reference workspace `AGENTS.md` for the policy text.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every in-scope filter / comparator / control-enum type has rustdoc covering exclusion + rationale + both future hooks (IETF-track + pre-IETF).
- Every affected crate's README.md has a Filter extensibility section.
- Workspace AGENTS.md filter-algebra exclusion is documented under JMAP-lbdy.10 (separate bead).
- `cargo doc --no-deps --workspace` clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean.
- `cargo test --workspace` clean (no behavioural change; tests must still pass).

## Decomposition

Per-crate rustdoc children mirror the JMAP-lbdy.1-.8 pattern (one bead per crate). Plus one sweep bead for READMEs since the wording is identical across the 7 crates.

  .1 jmap-types               (canonical foundation: Filter<T>, FilterOperator<T>, Operator)
  .2 jmap-mail-types          (canonical extension template: EmailFilterCondition + comparator)
  .3 jmap-calendars-types     (4 types)
  .4 jmap-contacts-types      (2 types)
  .5 jmap-tasks-types         (4 types)
  .6 jmap-filenode-types      (1 type)
  .7 jmap-sharing-types       (2 types)
  .8 README "Filter extensibility" sweep across the 7 crates

Cookie-cutter coordination: per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates", child .1 (jmap-types) and .2 (jmap-mail-types) are canonical. .1 should land first or in lock-step with .2-.7 to keep doc wording consistent across siblings.

## Relationship to other epics

- **JMAP-lbdy** (extras-preservation policy): this epic propagates a SUBSET of JMAP-lbdy's decision (specifically the filter-algebra exclusion, "Decision: filter algebra excluded" 2026-05-10) into rustdoc + READMEs. Does NOT depend on JMAP-lbdy implementation — pure documentation of an already-made decision.
- **JMAP-lbdy.10** (workspace AGENTS.md): expanded 2026-05-10 to also document the filter-algebra exclusion and the metadata-draft future-hook pointer. Sibling to this epic; the AGENTS.md text is the workspace-level statement, this epic's children are the per-type and per-crate statements.
- **JMAP-06zp** (tracker for `draft-ietf-jmap-metadata` implementation): rustdoc and READMEs here point at JMAP-06zp as the future-hook target. When JMAP-06zp ships, the rustdoc/README pointers should be updated to reference the concrete `jmap-metadata-*` crate types instead of the draft URL.
